headline: Discussed $2.0 million school budget surplus found at end of Fiscal Year 2026 and Fiscal Year 2027 budget changes.
summary: The Town Manager said an accounting error left about $2.0 million in surplus in the School Department budget at the close of Fiscal Year 2026. The interim School Department CFO reviewed the FY 26 results and the amended FY 27 budget of $65,421,429, up $229,768 from the adopted budget. The Superintendent confirmed that monthly budget reports will be sent to the Town Finance Director.

JOINT SPECIAL SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
1 
At an JOINT SPECIAL SESSION of the Town Council and School Committee of the Town of 
South Kingstown, County of Washington, in the State of Rhode Island, held at the Town Hall, in 
and for said Town on the 13th day of October 2026 at 6:02 PM. 
 
PRESENT: Town Council 
Rory H. McEntee, President 
Michael K. Marran, Vice President 
Deborah D. Bergner 
Patricia A. Alley 
Jay G. Wegimont 
 
School Committee 
Carol A. Vetter, Chair 
James L. Restivo, Vice Chair 
Michelle Brousseau 
Stewart A. Lander 
Kate M. Macinanti 
Paula J. Whitford 
 
 
Also present: James M. Manni, Town Manager; Amy H. Goins, Assistant Town Solicitor; Brian 
Silvia, Finance Director;  Michael Podraza , School Superintendent;  Daniel Seger , Assistant 
School Superintendent; Timothy McGrath, Chief Financial Officer, School Department ; and 
Anthony Ferrucci, Interim Chief Financial Officer, School Department 
 
1. SPECIAL SESSION 
 
A. The Pledge of Allegiance is given.  
 
B. The Land Acknowledgement Statement is read.  
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
3. NEW BUSINESS 
 
Council President McEntee introduces a Special Joint Session of the Town Council and School 
Committee. 
 
James Manni, Town Manager, reviews the reason for the Special Session and a brief timeline of 
events. He notes that due to an unforeseen accounting error, approximately $2.0 million in surplus 
was found in the South Kingstown School Department (SKSD) budget at the close of Fiscal Year 
2026. 
 
Superintendent Michael Podraza thanks the Town Council, School Committee , and staff  for 
accommodating the special meeting.  
 
Council Member Wegimont enters the meeting at 6:09 pm. 
 
The Superintendent explains what measure s have been undertaken to correct the sit uation. 
Interim Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the School Department Anthony Ferrucci has performed
JOINT SPECIAL SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
2 
an internal audit of the SKSD budget and adjusted expected revenues and expenditures in FY 
27. Timothy McGrath has been hired as the new School Department CFO. 
 
A. Anthony Ferrucci, Interim SKSD CFO, introduces the agenda discussion for the evening. 
He reviews FY 26 revenues and expenditures, noting that the net revenue was over budget 
$898,817 and the net expenses under budget $840,976.  
 
B. The Interim CFO next reviews the total Fund Balance of $5,358,907, comprised of the 
Assigned Balance of $1,303,833, which represents 2% of the Operating Budget set aside for 
emergencies, Committed Fund Balance of $1,003,292 for capital improvements, and Remaining 
Unassigned Fund Balance of $3,051,782. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to capital improvement funding , SKSD CFO transitions and 
changeovers, practices to  maintain the Assigned Balance , monies received for out of district  
student enrollment, the amended budget, Medicaid rei mbursements, and the Interim CFO ’s 
efforts to identify new billable services. 
 
C. The Interim CFO reviews FY 27 Revised Revenue: Total and Other  showing the Total 
Revenue, Tuition In, Earnings on Investment, Formula Aid, Medicaid, and Transfer In for FY 25 
Actual, FY 2 6 Budget, FY 26 Actual, FY 2 7 Adopted, FY 27 Amended, and differences. The 
amended FY 27 revenues total $65,421,429, up $229,768 from the adopted budget. 
 
He continues to review FY 27 Revised Expenses: Total and Staffing showing the Total Expenses, 
Salaries, Health Insurance, Medical Retirees, ESRI/MERS, and FICA for FY 25 Actual, FY 26 
Budget, FY 26 Actual, FY 27 Adopted, FY 27 Amended, and Differences (Adopted v. Amended). 
The amended FY 27 expenses total $65,421,429, up $229,768 from the adopted budget. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to General Fund budget transfers and the School Department’s use 
of a transfer of $1.5 million from the Town in April 2026. 
 
D. FY 2027 Capital Improvement Projects are not discussed. 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENTS 
 
Council President McEntee invites residents to come forward with comments. 
 
Jim O’Neill comments on  his disappointment with the School Dep artment budgetary errors, 
Medicaid reimbursements, and creative financial problem solving by Council President McEntee, 
the Town Manager, and Finance Director Brian Silvia. 
 
Bret Harrington comments on the April 2026 Budget Public Hearings, responsible school funding, 
the hiring of a new School Department CFO, and maintaining transparency. 
 
Jen Nerbonne expresses concerns over the budgetary surplus and emphasizes the importance 
of responsible financial decisions to provide quality education and keep taxes reasonable. 
 
Dorald Beasley comments on the 2023 Budget Referendum, School Department budgetary 
surplus, declining school enrollment, and regionalization of schools with Narragansett. 
 
Discussion ensues relative to scheduling another joint meeting  of the Town Council and S chool 
Committee in November.
JOINT SPECIAL SESSION 
 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
3 
The Superintendent confirms that monthly budgetary reports will be sent  to the Town Finance 
Director. 
 
UNANIMOUSLY VOTED: to adjourn at 7:35 pm. 
 
 
Emily R. Houle 
Town Clerk
